items.title: TAMCO, KILWA DC and MCDI Plant 100 Trees at Elishadai Primary School
items.excerpt: TAMCO in collaboration with Mpingo Conservation & Development Initiatives (MCDI) and Kilwa District Council (Kilwa DC), planted 100 shade and fruit trees at Elishadai Primary School while providing students with environmental conservation education.
items.content: On 28 April 2026, TAMCO in collaboration with Kilwa District Council Mpingo Conservation & Development Initiatives (MCDI), conducted a tree planting activity at the newly established Elishadai Primary School in Kilwa District. During the activity, a total of 100 shade and fruit trees were planted within the school grounds to enhance the learning environment, promote biodiversity, and contribute to climate change mitigation efforts. The exercise brought together students, teachers, and conservation practitioners in a shared commitment to environmental stewardship. In addition to participating in the tree planting exercise, students received environmental conservation education focusing on the importance of trees, ecosystem protection, and sustainable natural resource management. The session aimed to inspire young learners to become responsible environmental custodians in their communities. TAMCO and MCDI remain committed to supporting community-led conservation initiatives and promoting environmental awareness among future generations through practical and educational activities.

items.title: TAMCO Trains Women & Youth on Climate-Smart Agriculture in Kilwa
items.excerpt: TAMCO is training women and youth farmers on drought-resilient crops including sunflower and sustainable soil management, building long-term food security across Kilwa District.
items.content:
TAMCO is actively training women and youth farmers on climate-smart agriculture practices in Kilwa District and surrounding areas. The training focuses on practical, community-relevant solutions — including drought-resilient crops such as sunflower — that help farmers adapt to changing rainfall patterns and secure reliable incomes.

Participants also receive training in sustainable soil management, composting, and water harvesting techniques. By prioritising women and youth, TAMCO ensures that the most vulnerable community members become active agents of environmental and economic resilience.

items.title: World Environment Day Community Clean-Up — Dar es Salaam
items.excerpt: On World Environment Day, TAMCO and partner organizations will host a coastal clean-up and awareness campaign along the Msasani Bay shoreline.
items.content:
To mark World Environment Day 2025, TAMCO is partnering with Dar es Salaam City Council, TanzaBlue, and local schools to host a coastal clean-up and public awareness event at Msasani Bay.

Activities include beach clean-up, mangrove seedling giveaway, educational exhibitions, and a panel discussion on ocean plastics and marine conservation. All are welcome — families, students, and corporate teams.

Time: 7:00 AM – 12:00 PM. Refreshments provided. Bring gloves and closed-toe shoes.
